one_liner: Reducto turns PDFs, scans, spreadsheets, and other documents into layout-aware content or schema-defined JSON through a public REST API and an official MCP server.

auth.notes: A Studio-issued API key is the default integration credential and is sent in a Bearer header. OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange supports workload identity federation and authenticates as an organization, not as a delegated end user.

access.notes: On the hosted service, developers can create a free account and generate an API key in the quickstart or Studio. Standard includes $150 in free usage before usage-based billing applies. Deploying the document-processing backend in a customer-managed VPC or on premises requires Enterprise; running MCP locally does not self-host the backend.

api.notes: The public reference covers upload, parse, extract, classify, split, and edit, as well as job retrieval and deletion, asynchronous operations, and webhooks. Python, Node.js, and Go SDKs are optional.

mcp.notes: Reducto offers a hosted HTTP server and a local server distributed as `mcp-server-reducto`. The hosted server uses an API key and does not accept local file paths. The local server can upload local files to Reducto. Both expose document-processing tools.

verdict.rationale: Developers can create a free account and generate an API key without contacting sales. The public REST API covers the core document workflow, and Reducto offers an official MCP server for direct agent use.

evidence.quote: Create an API key in Reducto Studio (https://studio.reducto.ai) under API Keys. Signed-in readers can create one on this page.

The token exchange endpoint trades a subject token from your identity provider for a short-lived Reducto access token. It implements [OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8693).
An access token authenticates as your organization, the same way an API key does.
Sign up for a free account without leaving the docs.
Sign in to create a key here, or create one in Studio under API Keys.
Standard includes $150 of free usage, then list rates apply.
VPC and on-premise deployments are available exclusively for Enterprise customers.
Each capability is available as a standalone API endpoint or composed into pipelines.
Available in Python, Node.js, Go, and REST.
For parse/split/extract pipelines, the URL of the document to be processed.

The Reducto MCP server connects AI agents directly to Reducto. Once installed, agents in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, or any other [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) client can classify, parse, extract, split, and edit documents as part of their reasoning loop, without custom integration code.
The hosted server (mcp.reducto.ai) does not support local paths. Use a public URL or run the server locally.

problems: The detailed on-premises and hybrid VPC deployment guide required sign-in. The public Enterprise Readiness page confirmed availability, but private deployment requirements were not independently checked.

verification.note: The quickstart directs users to create an API key, while the separate OAuth token exchange authenticates as an organization rather than a delegated user. The quoted text does not establish the note’s claim about sending the key in a Bearer header.
A free account can create a key, and the pricing quote confirms free usage. The quotes also support the note that VPC and on-premise deployments require Enterprise.
The public docs explicitly identify REST and standalone API endpoints. The quotes do not substantiate every operation listed in the note, but do not contradict the breadth estimate.
Reducto’s docs describe a usable MCP server and identify a hosted server. The quotes do not establish all the note’s details about local uploads and authentication.
